*Reasoning in my own voice:*

Aiya, another spring. Let me think about this year. We have 8 mu — not much, but enough if I manage it well. My husband helps when he's not driving for the construction company in town, and my daughter-in-law helps with the cotton picking. The two grandchildren are in school so they only help on weekends and during the busy season.

I split my 8 mu like this every year: about 6 mu for wheat and maize together (the wheat is already in the ground since October), 1.5 mu for cotton on the sandy patch near the road, and a small 0.5 mu plot for watermelon close to the house — that one I sell at the roadside in summer, gives me a bit of pocket money.

**Wheat (already planted last October, 6 mu):** I planted the same variety as last year — Jimai, what most people in the village use. Before planting I put down about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu (the 15-15-15 kind), that's around 50 jin per mu. Now in spring I need to topdress with urea — I'll do one bag of urea (50 jin) split across two mu, so about 25 jin per mu, when I do the spring irrigation. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, hoping for similar this year. The wheat looks okay so far, not as yellow as my neighbor Wang's field.

**Maize (will plant mid-June, 6 mu):** Right after wheat harvest, very rushed — usually only 4-5 days to clear straw and plant. I hire the village tractor to come do the no-till planter, costs about 30 yuan per mu but saves so much time. I use Zhengdan 958 seed, what the seed shop sells most. Put down compound fertilizer with the planting, about 40 jin per mu, then topdress urea at the big-bell stage — maybe 30 jin per mu. If it doesn't rain I'll irrigate once or twice. Last year got about 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton (plant late April, 1.5 mu):** This is more work, my daughter-in-law and I handle it. I plant Jinmian variety, kept some seed myself but bought new this year. Cotton needs less water but more fertilizer over the season. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress twice. Picking is the hard part — three rounds in autumn, all by hand. Cotton price has been not great the last two years, but it's still worth it because the well water is enough and the sandy soil is better for cotton than wheat.

**Watermelon (plant May, 0.5 mu):** Small plot, I do it myself. Buy seedlings from the market in Quzhou town. Need lots of manure — I save chicken manure all winter from my chickens, plus a bit of compound fertilizer. Water more often when fruits are setting. If they grow well I sell them at the road in July-August, can make a few hundred yuan. If they don't, the family eats them.

Total budget for inputs this year is tight — maybe 2500-2800 yuan. My husband's off-farm work covers the household, but the farm money has to come from the farm. I always keep a few hundred yuan reserve in case the well pump breaks or I need to buy pesticide for cotton bollworm.
